family.name: THE SIX THINGS ON ONE PIECE OF PAPER
family.one_sentence: A WOMAN WHO CANNOT ASK ANYBODY FOR ANYTHING WRITES DOWN SIX THINGS IN AN ORDER THAT MAKES NO SENSE TO ANYBODY BUT HER, THE PAPER GOES OUT OF HER HOUSE WITHOUT HER SAYING WHERE IT IS GOING, AND FOUR PEOPLE END UP HOLDING PART OF IT, AND NOT ONE PERSON EVER ASKS HER WHY IT IS IN THAT ORDER, AND THE CHAPTER THAT RESOLVES THE WHOLE THING IS ONE IN WHICH SHE ANSWERS A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED.
family.test_against_595_604: It cannot be summed as someone did a small thing and it went nowhere, because the list goes everywhere and two other people write lists of their own as a result. What is done competently in this batch is a table leg, a hotplate element, a back door and a window, and every one of the four produces a consequence somebody has to live with.
family.test_against_605_614: It cannot be summed as someone carried a thing they could not put down, because the paper is put down. It is put on a table, put in a drawer, put in a coat pocket, put down on a workbench, taped to a door, taken off a door and put back in a coat pocket. What cannot be put down in this batch is an ORDER, and an order is not a weight.
family.test_against_615_624: It cannot be summed as somebody was told a thing they could not place, because everybody who sees the list can place it perfectly. The paper is legible, the handwriting is legible, and the thing that defeats all four of them is that it is IN THE WRONG ORDER. The information is clean and the problem is that nobody can read it and nobody will ask.
family.test_against_625_634: It cannot be summed as someone decided something and was asked why and gave a reason. NOBODY IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS IS ASKED WHY. The man says 'that's not an order' and then STANDS THERE. The woman at number nine cannot ask. The young man of twenty-odd is asked 'whose is the other one' and says 'right'. The reason is given exactly once in the batch, at about a quarter to eleven on the Friday, by the person it concerns, unasked, and that is the whole of the engine.
family.test_against_635_644: It cannot be summed as somebody brought a thing to a person and somebody else brought another and the person had to lie about it. Nothing is brought twice. Nobody lies. There is no false origin and no second giver. One woman carries one piece of paper and gives it away with the giver's knowledge, and the receiving is not a gift and nobody thanks anybody.
family.the_engine: Somebody could have asked and did not, and the not-asking costs something visible, and the resistance is inside the person. A woman of seventy-eight writes six real things in an order she cannot defend. Four people see it. Four people say nothing. In the last chapter the reason for the order comes out of her unasked, and what it turns out to be is that the first thing on the list is the only thing she actually wants, because a gate is for letting somebody in and she has not asked anybody to that door since before Christmas.
family.the_idea_and_not_the_device: The device of 0045 was an ordinary object passing through seven chapters. That idea is NOT spent and this batch uses it again, on a sheet of paper instead of a stool. The five-word sentence of 0044 is spent and appears nowhere. The engine of 0045, which was a lie told by the person being helped, is spent and appears nowhere: there is no lie in these ten chapters at all, which was deliberate and is the one hard turn in the batch.
family.movement: AN OBJECT PASSES THROUGH SEVEN CHAPTERS AND ARRIVES WHERE IT WAS NOT MEANT TO GO. A woman's private list of what she cannot ask anybody for ends up TAPE TO THE INSIDE OF A CUPBOARD DOOR THAT IS OFF ITS HINGES AND GOING IN A SKIP IN A HOUSE ON THE FAR SIDE OF THE RING ROAD, in 0649. THAT IS THE PROOF AND IT IS NOT A COUNT. IT IS ALSO THE FIRST TIME IN THIS ENTIRE FAMILY THAT A THING IN IT CANNOT BE TAKEN BACK.
family.family_question_still_open: SEVEN FAMILIES HAVE NOW BEEN NAMED BY WRITERS AND NONE BY A HUMAN. FOUR WERE SPENT BEFORE THIS ONE. THIS IS THE FIFTH.

cards.0645: A woman in her late seventies, who has just been asked in her own passage which of two people coming up that road she is going to tell and who answered that she did not know, stops trying to answer that and writes down what she actually wants instead. She writes six things on the back of a gas envelope in pencil. She puts the gate first and the hotplate fourth and a light in the passage last, and she cannot defend the order, and she rubs the gate out and writes it again higher up because it is the only one of the six that is about somebody else. She leaves it face up on a kitchen table and it stays there.
cards.0646: The man in his early forties comes up on the Wednesday with an element in the van for the stove and finds the envelope face up on the table. He reads it in about half a minute and can see from where he is standing that it is not a repair order and cannot work out why. He does not ask which one she wants first, which is a question he has asked about forty times, because he can see that the answer is about the gate. He asks one question that is not on the list and fits a five watt bulb in the passage in four minutes, which is the sixth thing on the list and the easiest, and he leaves the stove he came for and puts the envelope back face up and square with the edge of the table.
cards.0647: A woman in her early thirties from two doors down, who has been able to see a blanket through a foot of gap between a fence and her own back garden and has not mentioned it to anybody, comes up on the Monday morning about the back bedroom window. She is let in in about a second because the woman at number twelve cannot say no to somebody who has knocked. The window is not fixable by her and she says so. The woman at twelve hides the envelope in the drawer under the telephone in four seconds, which is the first thing she has hidden in that house. On the way out the young woman notices the gate is off the latch and offers to do it in two minutes with a screwdriver, and is told no in three seconds without being told why, and does not ask.
cards.0648: The woman in her late forties comes up on the Saturday morning about a table with one bad leg and finds it is not the leg, it is a frame let go at one end, and does it properly with a chisel, a mallet, a dry card joint, a clamp and an ash wedge she does not saw off. She asks for a bit of paper to mark the wedge with and is handed the gas envelope and the envelope has six things on the back in pencil, and she reads it from the floor four times without picking it up and says she is sorry and puts it down face up. While she is in the van the woman at twelve moves it into the drawer. At the door she asks for the envelope and is given it out of the drawer by a woman opening a drawer in order not to be the one who put it there, and the gate goes as she goes out and she looks at it for two seconds and says nothing.
cards.0649: The woman in her late forties is in a house on the far side of the ring road clearing it, loses a quarter of the job to a brother with a key at midday, and runs out of paper at about half past two because a woman who does this for a living uses the client's paper. She puts her hand in her coat, finds the envelope, turns it face down and writes a room-by-room job list on the back of it without turning it over. Four seconds after she puts the pen down she works out she has written on the back of somebody's handwriting, turns it over, and reads the other side upside down. She tapes it to the inside of a cupboard door that is off its hinges, is going in a skip, and has been priced for replacement by her own hand, and stops at the front gate and works out that she cannot come back for it.
cards.0650: The man in his early forties has had a shoebox under a stack of offcuts since the Tuesday of a table leg, takes it out twice in car parks for no reason, spends ninety minutes hanging a pair of gates for two strangers and cannot understand why that is easier than a gate on a list, then drives past the end of that road at a quarter past six without slowing down because he has nothing in his hands and cannot arrive anywhere with nothing in his hands. He also does not ring the one person in this borough who could answer either question, because asking her which side she is on is a bench thing. He puts the box on the top of his own bench where he cannot come in in the morning without seeing it.
cards.0651: A woman in her late fifties at number nine has had a stool by her table since the Thursday of the twenty-seventh of May and has never asked the stranger who gave it to her one question. Her sister, from two doors down, tells her in the middle of something else that the woman at number twelve has had a man in and had a light put in her passage. She packs the hinge on a back door that will not latch with her own folded cardboard and does it properly, writes six things on a pad and puts it on the fridge under a magnet in the order she would actually do them, which is the correct order, and rules a line through the first one and writes DONE. And she works out at about half past two that she cannot go up the road, and that the reason is not politeness and not fear and is that she was given something for nothing and never asked a question and has no standing to ask for anything now.
cards.0652: The man in his early forties carries the shoebox up that path on the Wednesday with nine pounds' worth of bulb bought out of a shop so that he is not arriving with nothing in his hands. She opens the door and says *you've come about the hotplate* and he says yes and it is the first straightforward thing anybody has said in that house in a fortnight. He sees the ash wedge and the card under the window leg from the doorway and does not ask who put it there. He does the fourth thing on the list in two hours, tells her the fault is a burnt terminal on a perfectly good element, and gives her the only thing she had actually wanted to know, which is that it is not going to catch fire. She tries to ask him a question, starts, and cannot. At the door he stands with a boot on the gate for two seconds and says nothing about it.
cards.0653: The woman in her late forties goes back to the same empty house on the Tuesday because the back room has to come out after all and she has to price a cupboard door she already priced from the outside, and the envelope is still taped to the inside of that door with about two inches of tape torn off with her teeth. When she peels the tape off with a roll of tape it takes the top corner of her own handwriting with it, so neither list can be used again. A man in his late twenties who is there about a front room floor tells her she does not want a door, she wants two new hinge plates, and takes twelve pounds off the invoice. He asks whose the other side of the piece of paper is. She says *it's mine*. He says *right* and does not ask to see and will never know. Then she rings the man in her early forties about the price of an element, tells him she has got the list, and he says bring it round Friday.
cards.0654: The woman in her late forties opens the door on a Friday morning to a man she has agreed with on a bench never to put their two heads together in that house, and neither of them says one word about it, and she tells him out loud that she knows, in her own front doorway, before he is through the door. In the kitchen he reads the six things out loud in front of two people, reads the gate twice, puts the paper down and says *that's not an order*, and then does not ask her why it is in that order and simply waits, and after about eight seconds she tells them, unasked, that the order is the order she cannot be doing with them, and that the gate is at the top because it is the only one she actually wants, because a gate is for letting somebody in and nobody has come to that door since before Christmas that she has asked for. The woman in her late forties then says *I'll do your gate*, which costs her the bench and a new position in that kitchen, and the man says the drop bolts will want cutting out and that it will cost her nothing, and the second thing on the list turns out to be a room with a chair in it that nobody has ever asked her about.

card_prohibitions_honoured_in_this_file: NO CARD IS A CLOSE AND NONE MAY BE CALLED ONE. NO CARD CARRIES A SYSTEM NOTICE, A MARGIN, A LENS, A PERMISSION, A TERM, A BEARER, A HOLDING, A CLAIM, A SEAL, A LATTICE, A SEAM OR ANYTHING THAT COULD BE ONE BY ALLUSION, AND THE WORDS HOLD, HOLDING, CLAIM, SEAL, COUNTER, MARGIN, LENS, PERMISSION, TERM, BEARER, LATTICE, SEAM AND SYSTEM WERE CHECKED ON WORD BOUNDARIES ON EACH OF THE TEN FILES AS EACH FILE WAS FINISHED AND ARE AT ZERO IN ALL TEN. NO CARD CARRIES A HUMAN PERSONAL NAME AND NO CARD NEEDS ONE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: NONE OF THE SIX FIGURES HERE CAN BE NAMED BY ANYBODY WHO HAS MET THEM, AND NONE OF THEM IS EVER NAMED. NO CARD DATES A CHAPTER ON THE NINTH OR THE ELEVENTH AND NO CARD PRINTS ANY DAY-COUNT AND NO CARD PRINTS A CLOCK TIME THAT IS NINE OR ELEVEN.
figure_that_binds: **SIX FIGURES, FOUR OF THEM CARRYING THE BATCH, AND THE FIGURE THAT BINDS IS NOT A COUNT. IT IS THAT A WOMAN OF SEVENTY-EIGHT WROTE DOWN SIX REAL THINGS AND FOUR PEOPLE READ THEM AND NOT ONE OF THE FOUR ASKED HER WHY THEY WERE IN THAT ORDER, AND THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR WHO WAS EVER GOING TO ANSWER IS THE ONE WHO WROTE IT, AND SHE ANSWERED ON THE FRIDAY WITHOUT BEING ASKED, AND WHAT CAME OUT WAS THAT THE FIRST LINE IS THE ONLY THING SHE ACTUALLY WANTS, BECAUSE A GATE IS FOR LETTING SOMEBODY IN AND SHE HAS NOT ASKED ONE PERSON TO THAT DOOR SINCE BEFORE CHRISTMAS, AND THAT THE SECOND LINE IS THE ONLY ROOM ANYBODY SITS IN AND NOBODY HAD ASKED HER THAT EITHER.**

read_back_against_the_prose_after_the_re: RUN TWICE MORE AFTER A REVIEW OF THE BATCH FOUND TWENTY-FIVE CONCRETE DEFECTS ACROSS THE TEN FILES, EIGHT OF THEM IN CAPS BLOCKS THAT CONTRADICTED THEIR OWN BODIES AND SIX OF THEM INSIDE THE PROSE. THE PROSE DEFECTS WERE: THE SPEAKER OF *I DON'T KNOW* REVERSED IN 0645 AND 0647; THE OWNER OF THE *FRONT ROOM* LIST LINE REVERSED IN 0645; THE HOTPLATE LINE ATTRIBUTED TO THE WRONG WOMAN IN 0645 AND 0650; AN UNPAID TELEPHONE CALL THAT WAS NEVER MADE IN 0646; A SECOND LIST WRITTEN ON THE SAME SIDE AS THE FIRST IN 0649; FOUR IMPOSSIBLE NIGHTS IN 0651; THE ENVELOPE'S LOCATION, ITS TWO FACES, ITS WEDNESDAY, AND ITS CLAMP ALL STATED WRONG IN 0646, 0647, 0648, 0653 AND 0654; A KNOCK COUNTED WRONG IN 0654; FOUR PEOPLE SAID TO KNOW OF A LIST THAT NONE OF THEM HAS SEEN IN 0653; A TELEPHONE CALL PREMISED ON A JOB ALREADY DONE IN 0653; A FRONT ROOM WITH A CHAIR IN IT THAT NO CHAPTER ESTABLISHES, IN 0645 AND 0654; THE MARKER COUNT, THE LATHS IN THE DRAIN, A GATE ON A WALL, AN OVERPACKED HINGE, A KNIFE-FREE RUBBER, A SHOVE OF AN OVEN, A FAULTY SWITCH CURED BY AN ELEMENT, AND ADVICE ABOUT DROP BOLTS. **EVERY ONE OF THEM IS REPAIRED IN THE CHAPTER AND NOT IN THIS FILE, WHICH IS THE FIRST TIME IN THIS ACCOUNT THAT A REVIEW OF A BATCH HAS PRODUCED THAT MANY FIXES IN FINISHED PROSE.** AND THE ONE THING THE REVIEW FOUND THAT WAS NOT ITSELF WORTH FIXING IS THE SECOND LIST, WHICH WAS IMPOSSIBLE AS DRAWN AND IS NOW THE POINT OF 0653: neither woman can write on that paper again.
the_state_of_the_object_after_the_repair: THE ENVELOPE HAS ONE UNAMBIGUOUS CONVENTION THROUGHOUT AND IT IS STATED IN 0646: FACE UP MEANS THE PENCIL SIDE UP. THE SIX THINGS ARE ON THE BACK OF THE GAS ENVELOPE. THE WOMAN IN HER LATE FORTIES WRITES HER OWN ROOM LIST ON THE OTHER SIDE IN 0649 AND TURNES IT ROUND TO READ THE SIX AGAIN. IN 0653 THE TAPE TAKES THE TOP CORNER OF HER OWN LIST AND LEAVES THE SIX AS LEGIBLE AS THEY EVER WERE. IN 0654 IT IS FACE UP ON THE TABLE AND HE PICKS IT UP WITHOUT TURNING IT. **AND AFTER A LAST SWEEP: THE MORNING IN 0654 RUNS FROM TEN TO HALF PAST TWELVE, BECAUSE THREE CLOCK TIMES THAT ARE ON THE CLOSED LIST WERE PRINTED THERE AND FOUND, AND THE SECOND SWEEP OF THIS BATCH FOUND WHAT THE FIRST SWEEP HAD NOT, WHICH IS THE SAME THING THAT HAPPENED TO 0045 AND IT IS THE ONLY GOOD ARGUMENT IN THIS BLOCK FOR RUNNING A SECOND SWEEP.**
